verdict.rationale: Dagster pipelines are defined as plain Python code and YAML config (assets declared as Python functions, components scaffolded into a project's defs/ folder with defs.yaml), created as a local project via the create-dagster CLI. That project can be self-hosted with OSS Docker deployment, and community reports describe a seamless laptop-to-prod workflow, which supports the code-first and portability parts of the story. Version control and code review of that code are only implied by it living in a project directory and are not explicitly documented, so coverage is partial rather than complete. missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of git-based versioning and pull-request review workflows for pipeline code, independent hands-on corroboration of moving the same project across environments.

support.subject: As a data engineer, my pipelines are plain code and config in my own repository — versioned, reviewed, and portable like any software

citations.quote: With Dagster, you declare—as Python functions—the data assets that you want to build.
An asset definition is a description, in code, of an asset that should exist and how to produce and update that asset.
